section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a single cross-sectional study of 387 women aged 18–25 who completed self-report questionnaires assessing early memories of warmth and safeness with peers, self-compassion, social safeness, body appreciation, disordered eating, and self-reported height/weight. Path analysis showed that early peer warmth/safeness related to higher self-compassion and social safeness, which in turn were positively associated with body appreciation, and higher body appreciation was associated with lower disordered eating.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The present study aimed to test the impact of early memories of warmth and safeness with peers, self-compassion, and social safeness, in body appreciation and in disordered eating attitudes and behaviours." "A total of 387 women aged between 18 and 25 completed a set of self-report questionnaires." "Early memories of warmth and safeness with peers associated with higher self-compassion and feelings of social safeness, which were both positively linked to body appreciation. Body appreciation associated with a lower display of disordered eating."
